note: Plain-English summaries compiled from public sources. Laws change: always check the official source before acting, especially before travelling with medication.

countries.summary: Cannabis-based products for medicinal use (CBPMs) can be prescribed by specialist doctors since November 2018, mostly through private clinics. Recreational cannabis is a Class B drug.
Medicinal cannabis has been prescribable since 2019, and the island licenses local cultivation. Recreational use is illegal.
Medicinal cannabis can be prescribed. Recreational use is illegal.
Medicinal cannabis prescribing and licensed cultivation are permitted. Recreational use is illegal.
Medical Cannabis Access Programme (from 2019) covers a short list of conditions; other access needs a ministerial licence.
Medical cannabis since 2017, taken out of narcotics law in April 2024 (MedCanG). Adults may possess limited amounts, grow at home and join non-profit cultivation clubs; no commercial shops.
Medical cannabis via the Office of Medicinal Cannabis since 2003. Coffeeshop sales are tolerated; a regulated supply trial is running.
Medical cannabis legal since 2018 and a major exporter to the UK. Personal possession of all drugs is decriminalised (2001).
A narrow medical framework for standardised preparations was approved in 2025. Private personal use is not a criminal offence; public use is fined.
Medical cannabis since 2018. In 2021 Malta became the first EU country to legalise adult home growing and non-profit associations.
Medical cannabis since 2019. Adults may grow up to four plants at home since 2023; public use remains restricted.
Doctors can prescribe medical cannabis without special permission since 2022. City-run adult-use pilot trials operate; minor possession is fined.
Medical cannabis available since 2013. Small-quantity possession is an administrative offence; further reform has been debated.
A state medical cannabis pilot has run since 2021 while a permanent framework is finalised.
Medical cannabis since 2007, largely supplied by the state pharmaceutical institute and imports. Personal use is an administrative offence.
Medical cannabis pilot programme since 2018.
Pharmacy-dispensed medical cannabis since 2017.
Medical access since 2001; adult-use legal nationally since 2018. A leading source of flower imported to the UK.
Federally controlled (rescheduling has been under review). Most states run medical programmes and about half allow adult use under state law.
First country to legalise adult use nationally (2013), via pharmacies, clubs and home growing.
Medical licensing since 2016 with a large export industry; a small personal dose is decriminalised.
Medical cannabis via TGA prescribing pathways since 2016. The ACT decriminalised small personal amounts.
Medicinal Cannabis Scheme since 2020; a 2020 referendum rejected adult-use legalisation. NZ flower now reaches the UK.
Private adult use and growing decriminalised (2018 ruling; Cannabis for Private Purposes Act 2024). Medical products regulated by SAHPRA.
Licensed cultivation for export; domestic use remains illegal. Ugandan flower reaches the UK via importers.
Long-running national medical programme; personal use decriminalised.
Delisted as a narcotic in 2022, then restricted in 2025 so that buying requires a prescription.
A 2024 law change allows approved cannabis-derived medicines; use is a criminal offence.
Strictly illegal, including prescribed cannabis from abroad. Check before travelling with a UK prescription.
Strictly illegal with severe penalties, including for residents using it abroad.
